target_customer: Authors and publishers selling eBooks through the large eBook stores, plus advertisers who wanted to target readers
problem: eBook stores shared only sales, ratings and reviews, so publishers could not see who read their books or how readers behaved. Hiptype wanted to be Google Analytics for eBooks and use that data for targeted in book ads.
business_model: B2B analytics platform with a plugin added to uploaded books, plus planned in book targeted advertising and campaign optimization

founders.name: James Levy
founders.background_notes: The YC description says the founding team previously designed and engineered products at Google, Turntable.fm and Chartboost, without saying which founder worked where.

founders.name: Sohail Prasad
founders.background_notes: YC profile text is a later bio listing him as a Thiel Fellow and later CEO of other companies. Education not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a plugin that could be injected into eBook files and report reader data back across several store formats, plus demographic inference; moderate for a two person team in 2012.

defensibility.rationale: The patent pending plugin was the only claimed edge, and it depended on the eBook stores allowing the plugin to run. The data would compound only with large reader volume.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The store owners already held reader data and TechCrunch noted they shared only sales, ratings and reviews; no source shows them copying Hiptype. Kobo published reader analytics for publishers in 2014.

market_need_then: TechCrunch's July 2012 launch coverage said publishers had only limited data from the big stores; the founders began after co-writing an eBook about big data. No customer counts or spend were found.

branding.domain_note: hiptype.com is the YC listed website; it did not resolve from this environment. Domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as Google Analytics for eBooks in launch coverage

branding.brand_signature: The tagline Google Analytics for eBooks
branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage by TechCrunch, The Next Web, Publishers Weekly and a Polish outlet in July 2012; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade press at launch but no sign of lasting recognition, and the name is easily confused with Hype or Hiptest style names.

outcome_analysis: Hiptype launched in July 2012 as analytics for eBooks and got a small YC investment; no later funding, product news or shutdown statement was found, and YC marks it inactive. The cause is not public. The model depended on the large eBook stores allowing a plugin and on publishers paying for data the stores kept, so the factors listed are inferred from the structure, not from a company statement.
notes: hiptype.com did not resolve (network restriction or dead). The $20K 2012 round rests on CB Insights alone; Seedtable gives a 1 Aug 2012 funding date with no amount. CB Insights also carries a mismatched office furniture description. No competitor was named in the TechCrunch launch post (only unnamed big eBook stores), and the rivals found in searches (Jellybooks 2015, Kobo 2014) are dated years after the batch, so the list is empty. Cause of failure not public.
